races.title: State Assembly, District 39
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Juan Carrillo
cands.bio: Democrat and city planner who has represented Assembly District 39 (Palmdale and the High Desert) since December 2022. He was previously a Palmdale City Council member and a Palmdale School District trustee, and worked about 10 years as a planner for the City of Palmdale.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists these 2026 endorsements: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, Equality California, Sierra Club Angeles Chapter.

cands.gaps: The sources I could read don't show any documented stance or action by Carrillo on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, growth limits, H-1B or immigration enforcement, policing, gun laws, abortion or school choice. His campaign site only says that on the Palmdale council he worked to expand affordable housing, address homelessness, increase green space and support small businesses. Ballotpedia says he did not complete its candidate surveys in 2022, 2024 or 2026, and the list of bills he sponsored did not load on the page I read. I found no documented controversies and no foreign ties. The sources do not give his birth year or the year he came to California.

local.label: Roots 80: His campaign site says he was born and raised in Guadalajara and immigrated to Los Angeles at 15, and he has since studied, worked as a city planner and held local office in the Antelope Valley.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since December 2022. Earlier he served on the Palmdale City Council (elected 2016) and the Palmdale School District board (elected 2013), and worked as a city planner, about 10 years of it with the City of Palmdale. He holds a master's in public administration.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service in the Assembly, local elected office and a planning and public administration career. The committee chair he holds adds nothing to the score.

cands.name: Paul Andre Marsh
cands.bio: U.S. Army veteran and longtime High Desert resident with a long career in the mortgage industry. Serves as a Victorville Planning Commissioner and has been a member of the city's Homelessness Solutions Task Force. Republican candidate for Assembly District 39 in 2022, 2024 and 2026.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (2026 Assembly District 39 race)

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Paul Marsh was born or raised, or when he came to the High Desert; his site says only that he has lived there for over 40 years. We also couldn't find which employers he worked for in the mortgage industry or for how many years. His campaign site gives only broad priorities (government spending, family, law enforcement), with no detailed policy pages. We found no stated positions or actions from him on data centers, development and growth, property taxes, institutional or foreign land buyers, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the pages we had.

local.label: Roots 55: His campaign site says he has been a High Desert resident for over 40 years, but it does not give his birthplace or say when he arrived, so the score uses the lowest tier his record supports.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Long career in the mortgage industry helping families buy homes, per his campaign site; also a Victorville Planning Commissioner and Homelessness Solutions Task Force member. No legislative or elected office is documented.
qual.why: A mortgage career is real-world work with some bearing on housing and budget questions, which puts him in the middle range. The planning commission and task force seats are civic boards and add nothing. No elected or legislative service is documented, and the career's length and roles are unknown.
